title: Occupancy-aware hillclimber for kernel fallback selection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our runtime currently picks kernels via a static ranking plus occasional microprobes. This struggles for mixed workloads where GPU occupancy and effective tensor shapes vary by architecture and sequence-length distribution, producing p99 latency spikes and suboptimal cost for long-prefill or long-decoder-heavy requests.

Goal: Build a lightweight online hillclimbing policy that maintains a small, per-arch+model fingerprint and safely experiments with fallback kernel choices when occupancy or seqlen histograms drift. The policy should favor low-risk probes, provide automatic rollback when latency regressions exceed SLO budget, and integrate with existing prefix/KV caching and batcher constraints.

Design summary:
- Fingerprint keys: (arch_family, model_shard_type, typical_token_shape_bucket, recent_prefill_mean, decode_mode) computed from lightweight sampling of requests.
- Reward metric: composite score prioritizing 95th/99th latency reduction, with a soft cost penalty (tokens/s inference cost estimate).
- Exploration strategy: simulated annealing / hillclimb iteration per fingerprint with staged probe sizes (first single-request microprobe, then small burst), bounded by safety thresholds.
- Safety net: probes are killed and candidate reverted if p99 or error-rate regresses by configured multiple of baseline stdev or absolute ms threshold for >5m windows.
- Rollout path: local microbench -> canary on <0.5% traffic -> ramp with SLA gating -> global release.

Why different from prior work: instead of a large bandit ensemble or expensive continuous probing across all kernels, this runtime-first approach uses architecture- and seqlen-aware fingerprints plus hillclimbing steps that prioritize stability and rollback, reducing probe noise and cost. It complements the kernel catalog and profiler outputs rather than replacing them.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Hillclimber controller component in runtime (Rust) with plugin points for kernel candidates.
2) Fingerprint extractor that consumes request headers and batch metadata.
3) Probe executor with phased probe sizes and telemetry reporting.
4) Canary orchestration in control plane and console dashboard tiles for visibility.
5) Playbook for rollback, troubleshooting, and tuning knobs.

Success metrics: 8-15% reduction in p99 for long-prefill workloads on heterogeneous instances, <=1% increase in overall cost per token, zero unmitigated SLO violations during ramp, and clear diagnostic signals in Console.

Non-goals: global bandit training, per-customer model retraining, or replacing the kernel catalog indexing system at this stage.
acceptance_criteria: Controller compiles and ships as feature-flagged binary in runtime-1.22 branch
Fingerprints generated at <1% CPU overhead and stored in ephemeral cache
Probe executor runs single-request microprobes and reports latency/cost metrics to telemetry pipeline
Canary rollout flow documented and exercised on staging cluster without SLO regressions
Console shows per-fingerprint rollout status and probe history dashboard
